correctness.rationale: Proof from the strict face-index rule partitions arcs uniquely into pair-indexed complete-tripartite blocks. All directed triangles are contained in one block; four-cliques are impossible. Blocks meet only at zero-cells, so the point-gluing lemma provides a wedge of circles/two-spheres, with no torsion. The 2-sphere sum equals binom(n-3,5) by a generating-function coefficient. Vertex, edge and face counts binom(n,3), 3binom(n,4), binom(n,5), plus connectivity, establish 5binom(n-2,3) circles. The proof checks n=3,4 and all n>=3; the standalone independent direct-construction bit-rank check passes n=3..11. Finite cases only corroborate the universal argument.

originality.rationale: The primary arXiv:2204.00462v1 introduces the exact strict n-path digraph and explicitly leaves homotopy of its directed flag complex as Question 3.33. It does not supply the all-n transitive-tournament calculation. Earlier directed q-connectivity differs by face-map/preorder construction. Full published Johnson-graph clique result has extra edges and trivial first homology and thus does not imply the positive-circle homotopy here. published-finding corpus searches of exact construction, aliases, equivalences and binomial ranks found no same or stronger statement; closest related IDs were compared at claim and implication level, not by title alone. Unindexed equivalent work is a residual risk.

value.rationale: The defining 2022 paper explicitly poses the classification of the homotopy type and Betti numbers of directed flag complexes of higher path digraphs (Question 3.33). For the canonical transitive tournament family, the theorem determines all n>=3 homotopy types with explicit positive circles and, starting sharply at n=8, two-spheres. This distinguishes the strict higher path construction from the original contractible tournament flag complex, upgrades Euler and finite calculations to integral homotopy and offers a reusable decomposition by tripartite join blocks. The result is not a routine parameter substitution or arbitrary finite graph census.
